name: MLC-LLM
notable_features: An ML compiler (TVM/Relax + TensorIR) ahead of the runtime, so a model is compiled to a per-target artifact rather than JIT-kernel-specialised at serve time
One MLCEngine behind Python, REST, JavaScript/WebGPU, iOS and Android, all with an OpenAI-compatible API
Platform matrix is genuinely broad: CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, Metal, OpenCL, WebGPU/WASM, OpenVINO-free
Published pre-compiled model artifacts on Hugging Face under the HF://mlc-ai/...-MLC naming, so no local compile step is required to start
WebLLM is the same compiler targeting the browser
hardware_caveats: Models must be compiled per target; loading a prebuilt artifact on an unsupported target means going through the compiler yourself
On Windows and Linux the Vulkan path requires a working Vulkan loader - the docs tell you to install libvulkan-loader via conda to avoid 'vulkan not found' failures

Hardware coverage is uneven in practice: the README's matrix marks AMD/NVIDIA Vulkan and CUDA, Intel Vulkan, Apple and AMD Metal on macOS, WebGPU/WASM in browsers, Metal on iOS, and OpenCL on Adreno/Mali for Android - but the rows mix targets, so 'supported' means a build exists, not that performance is competitive
The MLX-style compile step means model updates require recompiling an artifact; you cannot just point at a new safetensors checkpoint and serve
Throughput and features trail the CUDA-specialised engines on datacenter NVIDIA parts, which is the usual reason it is not chosen there
best_for: Deploying one model to many target classes - browser, phone, iOS, Mac, Windows/Linux GPU - from a single compile pipeline
In-browser and on-device inference with an OpenAI-compatible API and no server
Intel, Adreno, Mali or other GPUs without a vendor-tuned inference stack
avoid_for: Maximum datacenter throughput on NVIDIA, where a purpose-built CUDA engine wins
Rapid model iteration, where the compile artifact is a step between a new checkpoint and a running server
Anyone who does not want a compiler in the loop
notes: 'mlc-compiled' is MLC's own artifact format; q4f16/q4f32 are the published quantization variants (group-quantized weights with f16 or f32 scales).
